title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page. X = V/Π is a complex elliptic curve. G is the group of R-linear automorphisms of the real plane V that preserve Π and are orthogonal for the conformal structure. G^+ = G ∩ GL_C(V) = Aut(X,0), which is cyclic of order n = 2, 4 or 6. By the previous page, X admits a real structure iff det: G → {±1} is onto. In that case every element of G^- = G \ G^+ is an orthogonal map of determinant −1, hence a reflection, hence an antiholomorphic involution of X fixing 0.

This page has two steps.
(1) The set of real structures (fixing the origin) is the coset G^-. It is a torsor under G^+ acting by left translation.
(2) The question that matters is when two real structures are isomorphic, i.e. conjugate under Aut(X). G^+ acts on G^- by conjugation. For σ ∈ G^- and g ∈ G^+ one has σgσ = g^{-1}, so gσg^{-1} = g^2σ. Hence the orbits are G^-/(G^+)^2. Since G^+ is cyclic of even order, there are always exactly two orbits, and the centre {±1} acts trivially. Grothendieck's picture for n = 4 and n = 6 is the classical one: G = D_n acts on the fundamental square or hexagon, and the two conjugacy classes of reflections are the symmetries in axes through vertices and through edge midpoints.

The resulting 'Proposition' (heavily crossed out): when a real structure exists, G is dihedral D_n with rotation group G^+ of order 2, 4 or 6. The real structures fall into exactly two G^+-orbits, which are non-isomorphic by definition.

Grothendieck then conjectures how the two orbits relate to his families E_a and E'_a (a ∈ R_{>0}), presumably defined earlier. The guess is that for a unique a, one orbit consists of structures E_a and the other of structures E'_a.

Classical check:
- Generic real j, n = 2, G = Klein four group. The structures are σ and −σ.
  - j > 1728 (rectangular lattice Z + iaZ): the two structures are rectangular with ratios a and 1/a, both with two real components.
  - j < 1728 (rhombic lattice): both structures have one real component.
- j = 1728 (square lattice): one rectangular class (2 components) and one rhombic class (1 component), i.e. y² = x³ − x versus y² = x³ + x.
- j = 0: two classes, y² = x³ ± 1, both with one component.
This agrees with H^1(Z/2, μ_n) = μ_n/μ_n^2 = Z/2.

Purpose: this is preparation for the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' project, which classifies real and conformal structures on tori (and later on surfaces with boundary, cf. the disc drawings on the next page).
errors: For n = 2, G is the Klein four group, which is abelian, so the conjugation action is trivial; it is not 'non triviale' as written. There are still two orbits, now singletons, so the conclusion survives.

The Proposition's criterion as written ('conjugate iff the sequence 1→G^+→G→±1→1 is split') is muddled. Whenever a real structure exists the sequence automatically splits, since a reflection has order 2. The correct statement is simply that there are always exactly two isomorphism classes, indexed by G^-/(G^+)^2.

Only real structures fixing the origin (elements of G) are counted. Antiholomorphic involutions of the genus-1 curve X of the form z ↦ σ(z)+c, including fixed-point-free ones, are ignored. That is fine for real elliptic curves with origin, but not for real genus-1 curves.

The conjecture that the two orbits are 'E_a' and 'E'_a' with the same a depends on undefined notation. If E and E' denote the rectangular and rhombic types, it fails for generic j: there both classes have the same topological type, with ratios a and 1/a in the rectangular case. Only at j = 1728 are the two classes of different types.

ideas.what: Real structures on an elliptic curve (with origin) correspond to lattice-preserving reflections. They form a torsor under Aut(X,0), and isomorphism classes are G^-/(G^+)^2, always two classes when j is real.
ideas.modern_name: Real forms of elliptic curves; H^1(Gal(C/R), Aut(E)) = μ_n/μ_n^2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein; Alling; Gross–Harris 1981; Silverman's treatment of twists)

ideas.what: The two conjugacy classes of reflections in D_4 and D_6 (vertex axes versus edge axes of the fundamental square or hexagon) give the two real forms at j = 1728 and j = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Conjugacy classes of reflections in dihedral groups / real twists for CM curves

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct (modulo a slip for n=2) but classical computation of the real forms of a complex elliptic curve. It is exploratory groundwork for the surface-surgery notes and contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'L'une des structures réelles se particularise en deux orbites' should likely read 'L'ensemble des structures réelles se partage en deux orbites'.
'Je présume que si U est formé de structures E_a' should likely read 'Je présume que si l'une est formée de structures E_a'.
'(en [?] (pour n=4 ou 6))' is likely '(cf. pour n=4 ou 6)'. The phrase continues '...les symétries par rapport respectivement aux sommets et aux arêtes des polygones (carré, hexagone) fondamentaux'.
'est scindée (: discrets)' is uncertain; it may be '(i.e. ...)' or an annotation about the discrete case.
